why: `eval` runs its code where it is, in the workspace around it, once its argument is evaluated: after the code before it and before the code after it (MATLAB doc 'eval'), and a script runs in its caller's workspace, so what it assigns is a variable there once it has run (MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions'; the project's script-workspace rule, src/resolution/matlab-script-workspace.ts: a bare name's failed call that a script run strictly before it makes is kept dormant). Code `sprintf` builds is no text written where `eval` is, and still runs there, after `sprintf` has built it: in `runner.m` and `runner5.m` the script it runs makes `XV` before `XV(2)` reads it (dormant), in `runner3.m` `XV(2)` is read before the statement runs it (failed); and the run in `runner5.m` is a call of its own beside the call of `sprintf` (found by the step 14 second review).
